answer: Each identity etches a crystal signal pattern onto a shale tablet in the garden registry: the pattern is a hash of its work plus key and epoch. It locks an 80-credit bond and pays a 25-credit fee per identity. The garden keeper counts distinct crystal patterns; a repeated pattern, or a tablet whose hash mismatches its key, burns the bond; shale tablets cannot serve another key, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 distinct patterns, 80,000 locked and 25,000 in fees. Honest identities pay 25 once, bond back after a clean epoch. A cloned-garden ring fails because cloned tablets share one crystal pattern.
